title: Deep learning controls electrical stimulation patterns in human visual cortex
summary: A deep learning framework (a learned inverse network and a gradient-based optimizer) chooses electrical stimulation patterns for a temporarily implanted visual cortex device in a blind participant. The source states both methods outperform conventional calibration, reach targets at lower currents and give more consistent perception. The Neuron paper was published online 2026-08-07 and announced by ScienceDaily on 2026-11-10.
ai_technology: Deep learning inverse network and gradient-based optimizer for neural stimulation

evidence.tested: Proof-of-concept experiments in one participant with a temporarily implanted bidirectional cortical implant in human visual cortex.
evidence.unknown: Limited to a proof-of-concept study with one person, as framed by the source; long-term use not reported.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning model trained on trial-resolved neural recordings to synthesize and optimize stimulation patterns.
